headline: Back to Starbucks lifts margins on stronger comp sales
summary_short: Starbucks' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 8.8% y/y to $9.53 billion on 6.2% global comparable-store-sales growth, with operating margin expanding 180bp y/y to 8.7% and diluted EPS of $0.45, up 32.4% y/y.
summary_long: Revenue growth was driven by 6.2% comparable-store-sales growth (U.S. +7.1% on +4.3% transactions and +2.7% average ticket from delivery; International +2.6%), plus higher Global Coffee Alliance and licensed-store revenue. Operating margin expanded 180bp to 8.7% on sales leverage and lower store operating/D&A costs after reclassifying China retail as held for sale, partly offset by 'Back to Starbucks' labor investment. Net income grew a slower 33.0% than pretax income's 45.0% because the effective tax rate rose to 29.8% from 23.5% on China entity reorganization and held-for-sale reinvestment-assertion effects. No buybacks this quarter; board declared a $0.62/share dividend. One day post-quarter-end, Starbucks closed the sale of 60% of its China retail unit to Boyu Capital for $3.1B, keeping a 40% stake.

drivers.explanation: Consolidated net revenues rose 9% to $9.5B on 'Back to Starbucks' initiatives (Green Apron Service, menu innovation, redesigned Rewards program), with operating margin up 180bp to 8.7%.

6.2% global comparable-store-sales growth (U.S. +7.1%, International +2.6%) plus higher Global Coffee Alliance and licensed-store revenue; U.S. comps driven by +4.3% transactions and +2.7% ticket from delivery.
Tracks the operating-margin expansion described below against 8.8% revenue growth; also aided by lower restructuring charges ($25.1M vs $116.2M a year ago).
Sales leverage and lower store operating and D&A costs after classifying Starbucks China retail assets as held for sale, partially offset by labor investment supporting 'Back to Starbucks'.
not explained in the release beyond the operating-income drivers above; interest expense rose to $137.0M from $127.3M on higher borrowing costs.

Grew slower than pretax income because the effective tax rate rose to 29.8% from 23.5%, driven by reorganizing entities in China (~280bp) and an $8M discrete indefinite-reinvestment-assertion charge tied to the China held-for-sale classification (~110bp).
Tracks net-income growth (+33.0% y/y) against a weighted basic share count roughly flat y/y (1,139.4M vs 1,136.0M).
Tracks net-income growth (+33.0% y/y) against a weighted diluted share count roughly flat y/y (1,143.2M vs 1,140.0M).
No share repurchases during the quarter (per the equity statement); the small increase came from stock-option exercises and RSU vesting.
